summary: This program defines a RobotPet class that stores a name, battery level, and mood, then builds three separate robot pets and prints each one's details. It is a first look at how a class acts as a blueprint for many objects of the same shape.

lines.text: This begins the blueprint. A class does not hold any single pet's data; it describes the kind of thing a robot pet is.
The __init__ method runs automatically each time a new pet is created, and it receives the values you pass in the parentheses. The first parameter, self, refers to the particular object being built.
Assigning to self.name stores the value on the object itself, so it survives after __init__ finishes and can be read later as pet1.name.
Each object gets its own battery attribute, which is why Rover's battery of 85 does not affect Sparky's.
The third attribute completes the pet's state: a name, a charge level, and a mood.
Calling the class like a function creates an object and runs __init__ with these three arguments. The result is stored in pet1.
A third independent object from the same class, proving one blueprint can produce as many pets as you need.
The dot notation reaches inside the object to read its attributes, and the f-string drops those values straight into the text.
